fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Open Green Space; Detached Structure; Landscaped Area; Open Terrain
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Install a reflective address marker at the street to help responders locate the property quickly from a moving vehicle.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency apparatus to reach the front of the residence.
• Mark or designate a consistent parking area away from the driveway to prevent blocking the single access point during an incident.
• Keep the walkway between the driveway and front entry clear for responder foot travel.
• Trim any landscaping along the driveway edges that narrows the travel path or reduces visibility of approaching apparatus.
• Identify and mark any secondary foot path through the open terrain that can be communicated to responders as an alternate route to the rear.
• Post the address or a property diagram at the driveway entrance showing the location of the detached structure relative to the main residence.
• Keep a gate, door, or access point on the detached structure unlocked or secured with a combination known to local responders.
• Communicate the limited rear access condition to your local fire station so responders can pre-plan the property before an incident occurs.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Brush Area; Scattered Shrubs; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route; Grass Cover; Scattered Trees; Open Green Space
wildfire.recommendations:
• Clear dry or dead grass from within 10 feet of the house and any outbuildings.
• Thin scattered shrubs near structures so no shrub is touching or directly against a wall or corner.
• Remove shrubs growing in clusters between the house and the surrounding brush area to reduce connected plant material leading toward the structure.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees near the house so branches do not hang within 10 feet of the roof or walls.
• Keep grass mowed short in open areas between the house and the surrounding brush, particularly during dry months.
• Clear any dead or dry plant material from the brush area edges closest to the structure.
• Keep the single access route free of overhanging branches, tall grass, and encroaching shrubs along both sides so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate from the road under smoky or low-visibility conditions.
• Move any wood piles, stored materials, or debris away from the sides of the house and into open areas with short vegetation underneath.
• Maintain the open green space near the structure by keeping grass cut short and removing any shrubs that may be establishing in that area.
